2026-11-04.q: Which statement best captures the main point of the passage?
opts: The Government has agreed to raise its pay offer to 9.25% to avoid a strike.
Public sector unions have accepted a 7.75% deal but want more local bargaining money.
After rejecting a 7.75% pay proposal as inadequate, unions plan a second strike and stepped-up action, while both sides seek a way out of the impasse.

2026-11-04.q: What can be inferred about low-paid workers under the current proposal?
opts: Their actual increases would probably be much closer to the headline figure than under the previous deal.
They would receive a larger percentage increase than higher earners.
They are guaranteed a minimum increase of 17%.
They would be paid the local bargaining money first.
2026-11-04.exp: Kane notes "the absence of guaranteed minimum increases for employees earning less than €50,000", and that such provisions "had previously raised their increases from a nominal 9.25% to slightly over 17%". Without them, their rises would be close to the nominal figure.

2026-11-04.q: Why does the writer mention the summit of EU leaders in Dublin?
opts: To explain why the Government made its pay proposal.
To suggest that EU leaders will help to settle the dispute.
To show that the unions support Ireland's EU Presidency.
To highlight that the strike's timing makes it more significant and potentially embarrassing for the Government.
2026-11-04.exp: The writer adds, "Moreover, it coincides with a summit of EU leaders in Dublin during Ireland's EU Presidency" — "Moreover" signals an additional point that raises the stakes of the strike's timing.
